input.question: What must the first HealthForge prototype preserve when analyzing a public CMS prior-authorization source?
input.project_context: Illustrative local-development scenario. No patient, payer, provider, or customer information is included.

sources.title: MVP source corpus and support boundaries

applicability.rationale: The question concerns public source analysis and local-development controls described by the MVP corpus policy.

assumptions.statement: The prototype uses only public source material and synthetic examples.
assumptions.validation_needed: Confirm local test fixtures contain no customer or patient data.

exclusions: This example does not interpret CMS-0057-F or make a payer-specific recommendation.
PHI and production payloads are outside the MVP boundary.

summary.plain_language: The prototype should retain source provenance and stable citation locators while remaining inside the public, no-PHI MVP boundary.
limitations: This is a contract example, not a regulatory analysis.
A real Brief must use an ingested, versioned corpus snapshot.

findings.statement: A source is not retrieval-eligible until its artifact, checksum, retrieval timestamp, and citation metadata are recorded.

citations.locator: Definition of ready for the MVP
citations.support: The project policy defines the controls required before a source may be used in the first corpus release.

proposed_work_items.title: Capture provenance fields during local source ingestion
proposed_work_items.rationale: A future ingestion path needs the evidence controls described in the scoped corpus policy.
acceptance_criteria: A local source record stores a canonical URL, source version, retrieval timestamp, checksum, and stable locator strategy.
The record can be linked to a cited passage without storing PHI.

run_record.retrieval_configuration: Illustrative fixture; no retrieval was executed.
run_record.model_configuration: Illustrative fixture; no model was invoked.
